subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Tweezers and Switches
description: A quick win: understand DNA Tweezers and Switches.

hook.text: Add a strand and tweezers close — add the anti-strand and they open. DNA tweezers toggle between two states.

buildup.text: The first DNA tweezers were built in 2000 by Yurke — two arms connected by a hinge that opens and closes on command.

discovery.text: Fuel and anti-fuel strands drive the cycle — each closing or opening produces a waste duplex as a byproduct.

twist.text: Waste accumulation eventually poisons the system — after many cycles, the tweezers stop responding cleanly.

climax.text: Catalytic designs recycle fuel strands — reducing waste and enabling hundreds of switching cycles.

punchline.text: Open, close, repeat — DNA tweezers are the simplest nanoscale switch.

quiz.question: What limits the number of cycles DNA tweezers can perform?
options: The DNA strands permanently break after one use
Waste duplexes accumulate with each cycle, eventually poisoning the system
Temperature increases with each cycle, melting the DNA
